Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

practice noun and verb

doing something again and again to get better

also practise, rehearse, rehearsal, training, drill, practice makes perfect

classical

Cic. Lael. 17: egetque exercitātiōne nōn parvā
Sen. Ep. 83.4: vidē quid exercitātiō cotīdiāna prōficiat

exercitātiō, exercitātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

practice, training

Practice of any skill, not only of the body: exercitātiō dīcendī (Cic. Brut. 331, Lewis & Short). Traupman 258 gives Exercitātiō optima magistra est for “practice makes perfect”.

Examples

  • cumque ita balbus esset, ut ejus ipsīus artis, cui studēret, prīmam litteram nōn posset dīcere, perfēcit meditandō, ut nēmō plānius esse locūtus putārētur

    and though he stammered so badly that he could not say the first letter of the very art he was studying, by practising he came to be thought the clearest speaker of allCic. de Or. 1.260

  • Nec mē praeterit ūsum et esse et habērī optimum dīcendī magistrum; videō etiam multōs parvō ingeniō litterīs nūllīs, ut bene agerent agendō cōnsecūtōs.

    I know well that practice is, and is held to be, the best teacher of speaking; I see, too, many men of small talent and no learning who have learned to plead well by pleading.Plin. Ep. 6.29.4

  • At memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās

    ‘But the memory weakens.’ No doubt, if you don’t exercise itCic. Sen. 21

Other words

  • exerceō, exercēre, exercuī, exercitum — practise, train

    verb, second conjugation, transitive · classical · Cic. Sen. 21: nisi eam exerceās

    With what is trained as object (memoriam, vōcem), or sē exercēre, to practise.

  • meditor, meditārī, meditātus sum — practise, rehearse

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.260: perfēcit meditandō

    Of rehearsing what one will say or perform.

  • ūsus, ūsūs m. — practice; the skill that comes of it

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 6.29.4: ūsum et esse et habērī optimum dīcendī magistrum; Traupman 255: Ūsus est optimus magister.

See also exercise, experience, lesson.
